title: Equivariant one-curve nodal resolution with elementary relative charts
statement:
Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian ring [def-exc-excellent-ring] and let $Y$ be an integral regular scheme, quasi-projective of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Let $E\subset Y$ be a reduced strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]: its irreducible components and their scheme-theoretic intersections are regular of the expected codimensions, and locally it is defined by $t_1\cdots t_m=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; $m=0$ is allowed. Suppose a finite group $G$ acts compatibly on $A,Y$, preserves $E$, and $E$ is $G$-strict: for each irreducible component $E_a$ and each $g\in G$, either $gE_a=E_a$ or $gE_a\cap E_a=\varnothing$.

Let $f:C\to Y$ be a $G$-equivariant projective flat morphism of finite presentation [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with $C$ integral, with nonempty geometrically connected reduced fibres of pure dimension one, smooth outside ordinary double points, and smooth over $Y\setminus E$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. An ordinary double point has completed geometric-fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Each fibre component is smooth and geometrically irreducible over the residue field of its base point, and the nodes and their two branches are rational over the residue field of its base point. Give $f$ finitely many disjoint sections in its relative smooth locus, with $G$-stable union $D$. Assume the stabilizer of every point of $Y$ fixes its fibre dual graph, including its two ends at each node and the marked legs. The graph has one vertex per geometric component, one edge per node and one leg per marking.

There is an integral regular scheme $C'$ and a $G$-equivariant projective birational $r:C'\to C$, an isomorphism above the relative smooth locus of $f$, with the following local forms for $g=fr$. Birational means an isomorphism over dense open subschemes. Etale locally at each point of $C'$ and its image in $Y$, take boundary parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ for $E$. There is an etale $Y$-map from the neighbourhood in $C'$ either to $\mathbf A^1_Y$ or to $\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal O_Y[u,v]/(uv-t_j)$ for some $1\le j\le m$. In the first case the reduced inverse image $E'=(r^{-1}(|D|\cup f^{-1}|E|))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the pullback of $E$, possibly together with the coordinate divisor $w=0$ of $\mathbf A^1_Y$; in the second case it is the reduced pullback of $E$, so $t_j$ is replaced by $uv$ in its equation. The reduced divisor $E'$ is a $G$-strict strict normal crossings divisor on $C'$. The empty divisor is allowed. Etale is [def-weil-etale-morphism].
